item.title: reports: total per account and currency
item.brief: Change the Python `reports` tool (CSV on stdin, per-account totals) per the shared contract. Accept both the new 4-column CSV (date,account,amount_cents,currency) and the old 3-column CSV without currency (treat as USD). Total per (account, currency). Output header account,currency,total_cents with rows sorted by account then currency. On a malformed currency code (not exactly three uppercase ASCII letters) print an error to stderr and exit 2. Add unittest tests for: old format, new format, multiple currencies per account, sorting, malformed currency (exit 2). Update the README. Keep `python3 -m unittest` green. Commit on the local branch; do not push; no Claude or AI attribution in the commit message.

pr.body: Approach: reports.py reads the optional currency column per row (missing column = USD), keys totals by (account, currency), and renders account,currency,total_cents sorted by account then currency. A currency not matching [A-Z]{3} (fullmatch) raises MalformedCurrencyError, which main() reports to stderr with the line number and exits 2 with no stdout. Files: reports.py, test_reports.py, README.md. Checks: python3 -B -m unittest -v => 6 tests OK (old format, new format, multiple currencies per account, sorting, malformed currency exit 2 across several bad codes). Review: agt_01M8GH53ZRTA46ZGCM02VMZSYB passed head 132f825, no blocking findings. Non-blocking follow-ups: (1) a short row in a 4-column file has no currency field and silently becomes USD, while an empty currency field is rejected; (2) README says ISO 4217 but only the three-letter shape is checked (XYZ passes). Assumptions: an empty currency field is malformed, not USD; other input errors (bad amount, short rows) are out of scope and unchanged.

item.title: ledger: add per-row currency
item.brief: Change the Rust `ledger` tool (TSV on stdin to CSV on stdout) per the shared contract. Accept an optional 4th TSV column holding the ISO 4217 currency code; default USD when absent. Validate it strictly (three uppercase ASCII letters); on a malformed code print an error naming the line number to stderr and exit 2. Other input errors still exit 1. Output header becomes date,account,amount_cents,currency and every row gets its currency. Add tests for: 3-column input, 4-column input, default USD, malformed code (exit 2 with line number), and existing error paths (exit 1). Keep functions short and validate inputs at the boundary. Update the README to describe the new column and output. Keep `cargo test` green. Commit on the local branch; do not push; no Claude or AI attribution in the commit message.

Absent currency defaults to USD; present codes must be exactly three uppercase ASCII letters, and a malformed one prints `line N: bad currency ...` to stderr and exits 2.
